# Policymaker #192 — iteration 0022

Lineage landed through #188/#190 (commit 8d3403c). On main, `evaluate.py --check` exits 0 with no errors and lists only `baseline` and `challenges` as missing.
That result only checks the evidence index. Benchmark readiness is false, the benchmark has not been executed, and tool quality is still unmeasured.
[Iteration 0021 record](history/records/0021.json): #189 stopped as partial at the input budget (460k input in 18 turns, almost all on copilot/gpt-5.6-luna). Its work is saved at `ecd17c4` on `task/189` and is not merged.
I read the saved generator. The positive controls submit only 2 of the 50 or 141 required claims but expect `correct`, which breaks the frozen-denominator rule. The mutations are written as prose, not as actual submitted records. There is no per-ID expected ledger, and the README the report mentions was never committed.
I wrote [the repair order](orders.json) with `wake: true`. It starts from `task/189`, uses the small public cases (12/12/3 IDs), builds the actual mutated submissions, freezes per-ID outcomes, generates a README that maps each protocol row to its fixtures or to an explicit gap, and pins `challenges` as `prepared-not-reviewed`.
Expected gain: challenge fixtures that can be reviewed. The Verification runs without `LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT` and passes only if `challenges` drops out of the evaluator's missing list.
I updated [policy working memory](../policy/working-memory.md) with the landed evidence, the defects, the measured model use and how to continue.
Still incomplete: native fidelity, VI semantics, typedef-impact and diagram-difference coverage, isolation of withheld cases, and the baseline comparison. No readiness or product-quality claim follows from this work.

## What next
After the ordered task ends, read its report, its Verification exit code, the `models` block in its record (not the model it reports for itself) and the files that landed. Then order an independent review of the fixture expectations, preferably by a non-GPT model family, before any evaluator or scorer work.
Do not land `ecd17c4` unchanged. If the task hits the budget again, restore from its saved commit instead of redoing the work. Capability #169 and engine-change #165 are still waiting and must not block ready work.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
